stem: Key, Potion and Sword are modelled with interfaces (IItem, IUsable) rather than a base class because:
options: They share almost NOTHING - a common base would be the 2.5 is-a mistake; interfaces compose capabilities
explanation: A Potion is IItem AND IUsable; a Key is only IItem. Capability, not ancestry - the 2.7 lesson driving the design.

stem: item switch { IUsable u => u.Use(player), _ => "nothing happens" } uses:
options: A TYPE PATTERN (4.6) - act on capability, ignore items that lack it
explanation: The pattern tests IUsable and binds a typed variable in one step. Items without the capability fall to the discard.

stem: player.HealthChanged and player.Died let the world react while Adventurer knows nothing about:
options: The UI, sounds or achievements that SUBSCRIBE (4.3's decoupling)
explanation: The publisher announces; unknown listeners react. Adventurer stays ignorant of who cares - Observer in a game.

stem: Died fires only when health CROSSES zero. Putting that guard in the publisher means:
options: No SUBSCRIBER needs to de-duplicate - the event means exactly one thing, once (4.3)
explanation: Semantics in the publisher: 'Died' as a single fact beats every listener writing its own already-dead check.

stem: Rooms are nodes and exits are edges, stored as an adjacency list. This means the map:
options: Is a GRAPH - so 5.8's algorithms come free
explanation: The structure was not chosen to be clever - the problem IS a graph. Then twenty lines of Module 5 solve level design.

options: BFS with breadcrumbs (5.8) - shortest unweighted path, and the basis of a 'hint' command
explanation: The first step of that route IS the hint. Modelling the map as a graph made level-solving a library call.

stem: world.Reachable("Hall").Count is useful to a level designer because:
options: It answers 'can the player get everywhere?' - graph connectivity as QA (5.8)
explanation: A disconnected room is a design bug BFS finds automatically. Algorithms earning their keep in an unexpected place.

stem: Commands are a Dictionary<string, Func<string,string>> rather than a giant switch so that:
options: Adding a verb = adding ONE entry; the parse loop never changes (4.2's grown-up calculator)
explanation: Behaviour in data. Unknown verbs fall out of TryGetValue naturally - the 4.2 pattern at project scale.

stem: Connect writes the reverse exit too, so:
options: Every corridor works BOTH ways - an undirected graph (5.8); forgetting it strands half the map
explanation: The undirected-edge detail from 5.8, applied: go north then south returns you. A one-line omission with confusing symptoms.

stem: The text adventure is the course's densest INTEGRATION exercise because it makes load-bearing use of:
options: Interfaces, events, delegates AND a graph together in one program
explanation: Each concept is essential, not decorative - 2.7, 4.1-4.3 and 5.8 collaborating. That combination is the point.
